reviews.review: It's a solid game. I have been excited for this early access and it lives up to the hype in my opinion. Been waiting for rogue to come out for a long time now. As someone with 600 hours across different accounts on Deep Rock Galactic, and some time on DRG Survivor as well, I feel comfortable saying that rogue core exceeds my expectations for an early access experience. I enjoy the Hades-like experience of upgrades. For constructive criticism I experience occasional stutters perhaps due to dx12. Last thing I want to say is the game is difficult to get into. Sort of like getting past the first 100 or so episodes of one piece, once you play a few games and perhaps fail some runs like I did this game really takes off and fulfills my expectations.

It gets better with every update. Don’t listen those crybabies who disapprove of it for its high difficulty and randomness — that’s the whole point of roguelike games and as a roguelike game, Rogue Core is really fun and good. Right now it heavily lacks customization and some unique events, but it’s early access. They already fixed some critical bugs and, as I see, listen to their community, so keep going GSG.

I LOVE DRG, got over 1300 hours in it, and I love roguelikes! So what can go wrong?

Well the worst for me are the upgrades you get during a run. Most of them are rather boring, and it's really hard to make a decent build during a run. I only had one run so far where I actually got some synergies for my character, and even though I'm a greenbeard in this game, I immediately got double the kills of anybody else.
And this can't be fixed with a small update, this has to be a major overhaul.

Another issue that got me to stop playing for now, is that every mission is the same. In DRG you have many different types of missions, and you can just pick those that you like. In this game it's just a difference in how many levels you have to go down before you get a boss battle. Sure you got some events or mini-games along the way, but DRG has those too. And every floor you do the same; find the bio-booster, fix the workbench, etc.

Biomes are straight from DRG. I thought that we were going waaay deeper this time, but then you still get the Dense Biozones or the Crystalline Caverns? What a letdown.

Now I do believe in these devs, so I hope they will fix this game. But for now, I do not recommend it.

Rogue Core is a very hard game. Rogue Core is a very punishing game. But in my experience, it is also an incredibly fair game.

There are so many times when I have failed a run and immediately went "Yeah, that was my bad. I shouldn't have done that." And I feel that mainly comes from the incredible amount of choices the game forces you to make. 
Should you pick the gun you're familiar with, or grab something that better fits your current build? 
Should you go run for that workbench, bio-booster, when the timer is already this close to being in the red? 
Do you run for that ammo crate in the middle of a swarm or do you try to hold out with what you got left?
Do you grab an upgrade that you could really use for your build, or do you grab health, because you're really low and about to get swarmed?

I feel like so much of the game is about trying to make the best of what little you have, and that's what makes it so engaging to me. I also feel that the weapons are fairly well balance, and clearly excell in certain areas, while struggling in others. For instance, the charge pistol (my beloved) is fantastic for taking out larger enemies and bosses, but SUCKS at dealing with many smaller targets. I also love how you can use the characters enhancements to further narrow down your playstyle for every class, and I especially love that I can stack multiple instances of health, armor, or crit damage to try and min-max my build (dealing more than 8000 damage to a boss in a single shot feels absolutely incredible).

That is not to say that there aren't problems, of course. Needing to wait for everyone to gather around the drone is rather tedious, and the game requires proper coordination and communication for you to get anywhere (which is why I've exclusively been playing with my friends in a voice call). I've also been having some connection issues from time to time, and nothing has gotten me quite as rattled up as getting disconnected from a game just as a swarm was starting to spawn.

But I am fairly confident that any issues will be fixed over time. The devs have made it very clear that they are open to feedback and criticism, so if there is something you don't like PLEASE fill out the form and let them know.

TL;DR The game is really fun with friends and challenging in a good way. I would highly recommend it to anyone that likes coop games and rogue likes ^^

A lot of the things people are complaining about (like the timer, shared upgrades, ammo economy, etc.) are really not as bad as people make them out to be, at least in my opinion. Yes, these systems definitely could have been implemented better, and that's what Ghost Ship is working on now, but saying they're all bad and should be completely removed sounds to me like you were expecting it to be exactly like DRG classic, which they explicitly said it wasn't. The timer adds a level of intensity and challenge, forcing you to be efficient with looting the level and adding to the feeling of being elite forces on a special ops mission. The shared upgrade negotiations are definitely better on a team of friends than with randoms, but you can "call" an upgrade before it's your turn to pick, and in my experience so far, most randoms will respect that. The ammo economy issue is really nonexistent for me. So long as I top up with any ammo available before continuing through the level, even if I don't fully need it (which the tutorial literally tells you to do), I pretty much never run out.
In my opinion, the bigger issue right now is a lack of variety, and not just in the amount of "stuff" (enemies, upgrades, weapons, etc.), but more so in the core gameplay loop. Right now there is really only one mission objective, so it starts to feel a little samey after a while. That said, I'm still having a lot of fun with it, and while I don't agree with all of their design choices, I see the vision behind them and can respect that they wanted to try something new.
If you're looking for DRG 2 in this game, you will probably be disappointed, but if you'd be interested in a more challenging, tactical experience combined with DRG's destructible terrain and visual style, I recommend giving this a try.

While this game is still in development; It comes from the same studio that brought about Deep Rock Galactic.  This game has their attention and wishes to improve on the model they made public not long ago, so many of this game's flaws (like what they listed on their day 1 reflection post) are being reworked at this time.  Basically speaking on this game's structure: Smaller, more simple DRG experience with an emphasis on time, surviving swarms, and putting it all on a dice roll that gives players near total freedom to be what class they want with what weapons they prefer.  It has RNG working against you sometimes with bad card drafts or the cave structure being more maze-like than in the classic DRG experience, and the enemies can be ruthless to people who tend to lag behind on missions.  The biggest upsides I see is that the dev's doubled down on DRG's later updates that included synergies between elements, and the classes they have here are all equally capable of taking on challenges on their own or with a squad.  More elemental reactions are present here, all weapons can tap into elements easily, and these classes have abilities that can make light work of waves, bosses, or even objectives.

After the first update went live: this game had many adjustments that transformed the experience into a fun and more enjoyable time.  There are way more choices for the general upgrade pool that have you change your approach to given situations; such as damage blocking, armor generation, and elemental archetypes that weren't in the initial release before.  They also reworked existing cards to be more worthwhile getting than their initial models; like the super-strapped artifact losing it's only downside (reduced movement speed).  The developers also gave players a sort of challenge selector for each mission you boot up, so now players have choices for longer timers to loot in each stage, the default timers for the original experience, and a shorter timer than missions would have normally.  They all enhance experience gained during missions, and the bonus only gets better as you shorten those timers.  I love the freedom to choose the lengths of time!  Now I can explore more freely without being punished as much as before, and I can work up to doing missions with more difficulty like they have bragging rights!  All these changes make playing the game feel so much different than my first take, and now it feels so well tuned that my impressions on each class feels equal to each other in performance.  Even playing as the Spotter feels better now that there's more options to play around crits than just increasing damage.

I was already on board with the game's model, but I feel that the game's only going to improve and become more fun going forward!  I welcome anyone to give this game a shot now that the biggest issues have been worked around.  This game already feels like if DRG was more speed oriented and less burdened by resources like the magnites or jadis.  Even the bosses feel like they've improved from dreadnaughts before; being more dangerous and harder to takedown than prep-work alone.

Rogue Core just needs... time. Some fixes and changes are on the way and they're great! But... The game really emphasizes a lot of the much smaller issues I had with DRG. In DRG it wasn't a big deal if enemies kept coming another 15, 20 seconds after a wave 'ended'. Here it does. In DRG it wasn't too big a deal if an enemy hit through some terrain you couldn't attack them back through. Here it does. In DRG, it wasn't too big a deal if your character slipped off an easily mantle-able ledge for seemingly no reason. Here it does. I'd argue I seem to slip off ledges more now than I ever did in DRG.

Every small setback or annoyance with DRG's mechanics is emphasized here atop new issues, such as the q+input sometimes just... not working when I press them too fast, same for power attacks. I think things like balance and such will be ironed out into enjoyable states for everybody and I'm not really worried about that. But if these issues that result in big punishments for the player in Rogue Core don't get touched up, I don't know if I'll be able to give it the same love and attention I gave DRG.

Right now I'm feeling pretty sad that updates for DRG came to an almost complete stop for this, it doesn't feel like it was worth the wait. Hopefully (and most likely) the game will change for the better and I can delete this review. If you're a player new to the series, check out DRG, still plenty of content for a new player-- and check back here in a few months.
